time.desc: The country officially confirmed the completion of the succession of the wartime top leadership. The new top leader made his first public appearance in the highest capacity and received loyalty mobilization.

Opponent’s security circles openly admitted that there was no feasible regime change plan before the air strikes, and shifted the focus of the conflict to discussions on the whereabouts of sensitive nuclear materials and seizing plans.
The opponent carried out air strikes in the area where the country's key energy export hub is located, targeting air defense and naval related facilities.

Senior officials of the counterparty publicly stated that they have no objection to the passage of ships from some countries through strategic waterways, and linked subsequent energy market intervention to the duration of the conflict.
The country confirmed that another top official was killed in an airstrike, becoming one of the highest-ranking officials to be purged since the war began.

The coalition launched a new round of air strikes on the country's large offshore gas fields and continued attacks on energy infrastructure. At the same time, rival leaders said they would end the war soon and navigation of strategic waterways was effectively blocked.

The top leader of the opponent party issued a time-limited ultimatum to resume commercial shipping in the strategic waterway or else it will hit the country's critical infrastructure such as electricity.
The country’s armed forces publicly warned that if opponents attack energy facilities, they will take escalating counterattacks, including the complete closure of strategic waterways.

Counterparties announced that they had entered into dialogue with the country and committed to a short-term pause in attacks on energy facilities, and officials from the country later confirmed that negotiations were ongoing.
Adversaries formally submitted a multi-clause end-of-conflict plan to the country to advance ceasefire negotiations

The country issued a formal written response to the opponent's ceasefire plan, bringing negotiations to a new stage. At the same time, the opponent reported the killing of a senior naval commander responsible for the strategic waterway blockade.
Adversaries jointly carried out military strikes on the country's key docks near strategic waterways, causing casualties
Major countries outside the region have proposed alternative framework plans for ceasefire and restoration of strategic waterway traffic in an attempt to promote the process of ending the war.

The top leader of the opponent's side made a nationally televised address, announcing that he would crack down on the country more severely in the coming weeks and reiterated the goal of ending the conflict as soon as possible.
Adversaries launched joint air strikes on the country's important petrochemical industrial parks and export ports, causing injuries.

The top leader of the opponent side publicly threatened to attack the country's civil infrastructure such as power and transportation and demanded the opening of strategic waterways. The country's top advisers warned that the blockade of another key waterway may be escalated as a counterattack.
Counterparties agreed to initiate a ceasefire lasting about two weeks and suspend bombing of the country, and the market risk premium fell rapidly.

Key differences emerged over the scope of the ceasefire: one party made it clear that the ceasefire did not restrict its actions against relevant armed groups in the country, while the other side urged that the organization be included in the ceasefire

The country held a periodic national memorial service for the slain supreme leader, and the new supreme leader delivered a speech reinforcing the resistance narrative, while the dispute over the fees and rules for strategic waterway access escalated

The opponent's military officially launched a naval blockade of the country's ports and stated that it would not affect navigation at non-country ports, causing the prospect of a ceasefire to become unclear again.

The leader of the attacking side publicly questioned the life and death of the new supreme leader of the attacked side and said that he had sent a letter to the other side to promote nuclear negotiations.
The leader of the attacking party publicly called on all countries to go to the key straits to rush for oil, claiming that the attacked party had basically been defeated.
Country Y The navy mobilized forces to Strait A in preparation for a blockade of the port of Country X
